profile.name: Pounce Light
profile.description:
Pounce Light AB is an independent Swedish game development studio registered in Sweden (identification number 559399-6761), founded in 2022 and headquartered in the Stockholm/Segeltorp area. The company develops and publishes a single PC video game - Tiny Glade - sold exclusively through Valve's Steam storefront for Windows, Linux, and macOS (Apple Silicon only). The product targets casual gamers and creative enthusiasts seeking low-pressure creative expression, with no objectives, timers, or failure states; players "doodle" whimsical castles, cottages, and ruins as a relaxation activity.

Technically, Tiny Glade is built on a Vulkan-based rendering pipeline with extensive driver workarounds for AMD and NVIDIA GPUs, a proprietary auto-save system that retains local backups at approximately 5, 10, 60, and 120-minute intervals plus pre-crash snapshots, and Steam Cloud synchronization. The studio operates a daily-themes content service served from Hetzner-hosted infrastructure in Germany, a custom in-game crash reporter that ships telemetry (OS, hardware, GPU state including NVIDIA Nsight Aftermath, minidumps, gameplay event log) to Sentry, and custom cursor rendering added in version 1.14.3 to handle OS-level cursor visibility issues. Cloudflare provides website hosting, and MailerLite powers a double-opt-in monthly newsletter.

Commercially, Pounce Light runs a product-led, one-time-license model: revenue is generated solely from Steam purchases of Tiny Glade, with no subscriptions, DLC, or in-game purchases disclosed. The studio has 1-10 employees, no disclosed institutional funding, no parent company, no subsidiaries, and no second product line; Anastasia Opara is listed as co-founder.

profile.name: Aggro Crab
profile.description:
Aggro Crab is a privately held, founder-owned independent video game studio founded in January 2019 in Seattle, WA, by Nick Kaman and Caelan Pollock, operating as Aggro Crab Games LLC under Washington jurisdiction. The studio develops and publishes original games across multiple genres, building on the Unity engine and shipping simultaneously to Steam, Xbox (including Game Pass), PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, and Epic Games Store. Its portfolio comprises five core titles: Going Under (2020, published by Team17, a satirical roguelike dungeon crawler about failed tech startups), Another Crab's Treasure (2023, a soulslike adventure with a trash-as-shell mechanic), Peak (2025, a co-op survival climbing game co-developed with Landfall Games that has sold over 10 million copies), Crashout Crew (2026, a physics-based 4-player co-op game), and Subway Midnight (2021, developed by Bubby Darkstar). Peak's 1M first-week and 10M+ lifetime sales are the commercial anchor, with ongoing player engagement tracked through Unity-based anonymized telemetry for balance and bug-detection purposes only — the studio does not collect personal data or run ad targeting.

The studio runs a lean operation with a team of approximately 15 and no disclosed external funding. Revenue is generated primarily through one-time game purchases on digital storefronts (e.g., Going Under at $19.99, Subway Midnight at $9.99) supplemented by Microsoft licensing fees from Xbox Game Pass day-one releases (Peak, Crashout Crew, Aphelion, Beastro). Go-to-market is product-led and community-led: titles gain traction through platform visibility, Discord community engagement, and organic social (TikTok, YouTube, Bluesky) rather than paid advertising or enterprise sales. Distribution is handled in-house for most titles, with Team17 retained as the legacy publisher for Going Under and Landfall Games as a co-development partner for Peak. The studio's positioning centers on humorous, accessible gameplay that subverts genre conventions — accessibility options, satirical tone, and a "BE AGGRO BUT ALSO KIND" brand ethos — and its games span difficulty scores from 2/10 (Another Crab's Treasure with assists) to demanding roguelike and soulslike experiences.

profile.name: LocalThunk Inc.
profile.description:
LocalThunk Inc. is a privately held, solo indie game development studio based in Canada, founded in 2021 and operated by a single founder who previously worked in IT. The company develops and self-publishes the Balatro franchise, a poker-themed roguelike deck-building video game built on the Love2D framework with Lua scripting. Balatro's core design combines a CHIP X MULT scoring mechanic with 150 collectible Joker cards featuring synergistic effects, layered meta-progression (stake levels, vouchers, boss blinds, achievements, challenges), and a deliberately low-stakes, "jazz solitaire" aesthetic with no player character or health system. The game was designed without reference to existing deckbuilders to preserve an original feel.

LocalThunk's business model is one-time digital game sales (~$9.99 on Steam, with platform-specific pricing on consoles and mobile) supplemented by branded merchandise sold through partner Fangamer. The studio does not operate subscriptions, microtransactions, or freemium mechanics. Day-one distribution across Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and (later) mobile is enabled by publisher Playstack, which handles marketing, localization, porting coordination and press relations; port development is credited to Love2D expert Maarten De Meyer, and the soundtrack was composed by Luis Clemente (the only external development spend). The mobile port launched in late 2024 as a follow-on expansion of the addressable audience.

Go-to-market is product-led and community-led: discovery was driven by organic streamer coverage (Dan Gheesling, Northernlion, Hafu), two consecutive Steam Next Fest appearances (October 2023 and February 2024), a nine-month public beta with active Discord engagement, and an invitational streamer tournament in January 2024. Critical reception at launch was strong (PC Gamer 91/100, Metacritic and OpenCritic 90+), and the developer continues to publish long-form blog content (localthunk.com) and work on a free 1.1 update. The company has no institutional funding, no parent entity, and no disclosed headcount beyond the founder.
